# Second pass: do not freeze yet

Everything below is from reading the texts; I ran nothing. Where I checked something by hand I say so.

## 1. The ten required changes

All ten are carried out. None is carried out wrongly, but several open new defects.

- **Values specificity is undefined.** Claim 4.2 and D2 5.1 ask for "fewer than two of Y′" in the run with Y. In values Y′ has no places in that run. Say that in values the condition is only "the run with Y′ has two of Y′", with condition 3 and X alone standing in for the rest.
- **C(r) and CF(r) leave the base law unquantified.** "COPY-LAW(t) or CAP-3(t)" does not say whether one law is fixed for the whole class (claim 4 says "one law") or any law per member. Write C(r, base law). Say CF is under MET only and STEPS-1 is reported.
- **The form class mixes the two families.** "The same X for every Y" cannot run over 𝒴_made and 𝒴_start together. Make it two classes. Note that made-3's Y and three-222's Y are the same pattern.
- **P2 (check) leans on S6 for every start.** The third-pattern starts give e three holders, so S6 does not cover them. Compute their tie classes at round 0 and say so.
- **P16 has a gap** (see 3, B3).
- **P5's wording is wrong.** "Made members made by offshoots of start knots" should be "are offshoots of start knots". Its second clause (no renaming of Y's knots) needs one more line than S4: a taken distinction always keeps its old holder outside the set.
- **Claim 5 overstates by one case.** "Holds one loose distinction" should be "at most one", since an implied birth holds none.
- **X alone is compared by names.** D2 4.6 compares X's course across two differently numbered starts (X = {1, 2} against {2, 3}). It must be the trace renamed by first appearance.

The two disagreements:

- **The place moving from 16 to 10.** The drafter is right about the place: with Y barred, Y's join is not made, 16 keeps one holder and is not eligible, and 10 is the largest eligible name. Names of made distinctions also move (52, 53 become 34, 35, because Y's joins are named before X's offshoots). Both are true and the conclusion is the same, so it does not matter.
- **B(ii) on start knots.** The drafter is right that FD's text leaves it undefined; the fold engine's extension is not FD. It does not matter, but say once that B(ii) is not run here, since P1, S1 and item 10 still mention it.

## 2. The form arm

- **The class is sound after two fixes.** Dropping only makes CF easier to satisfy, and CF is predicted to fail, so the drop is conservative. The fixes: split by family, and say the class follows the engine's census, not the prototype's.
- **The census is too weak to give the negative meaning.** It counts parts of any descent in any design. Also report, per member, whether any run makes one part the same as Y with every member descended from X only. Without that, "X failed to leave two" and "X's descendants never make that pattern at all" are not told apart.
- **The controls of the readings are not enough.**
  - The Y's-knots search stops at two renamings, but P14 asks for counts up to 24. A counting mode must be defined, and what it counts.
  - The planted part and planted knots are not defined anywhere.
  - Form has no every-choice control; run 4 is values and parity only. So a form negative says "four rules and their swaps do not", not "the law does not allow it". Either add form to run 4 as a reported reading, or say this under "would not show".
- **CF(r) is decidable** once the base law is quantified: one member without two decides it.
- **"One specific case" is not honest as written.** The disclosure shows that with made-3, made-5 and made-6 there are no two of the new Y. That is failure on the class, not specificity. D2 5.1 needs the reverse: fewer than two parts the same as made-4's Y in those runs. That is not stated.
  - B(i) gives the same two, so the case does not need Y's births, only Y's knots.
  - It is lost under n1, n3, the order of births reversed and HOLD.
  - Honest wording: "one case that is there with this Y and not in X alone, not a copier for any other member, lost under renaming".

## 3. The owner's arm

**The definitions**

- **Ended.** D2 adds "none was made in round T" to SD line 91. A pattern whose last birth is implied then counts as "goes on" though it has no member. Use SD's ended, and define "goes on" as a member left and a birth in round T.
- **The round.** D2 says "at run A's last round"; the note says B(i)'s if earlier. Use the last round both reached (D2 4.8).
- **"Ended by what it met" requires no meeting.** Either require confirmation through a meeting (M) or rename it. Its comparison is against Y barred, not Y absent, so what ends X is Y's births after round s.
- **The bound.** "Not ended in B(i) at T" can mean ended one round sooner. Report the round of ending in both runs.
- **Plainness.** "Goes on is not for ever" is said plainly. Say equally plainly: "ended with Y making births, not ended by round T with Y barred".
- **Fairness to "break out".** Not fair; see 4.

**B1**

- (a) Right, by S1.
- (b) Right.
- (c) Wrong as summarised. Y's births can make X's member short; under CANCEL-RETIRE it retires and its loose distinctions are barred. The barred marks change, through X's course. Also missing from "barred only by": FILLERS and the barring of the paired runs.
- (d) Right only as "no birth without a parent among X's members takes them"; joint births and retiring still change them.
- Fix P2 item 7 and claim 6(ii): "no place, no relation among existing distinctions; holders of shared distinctions, and through the course which loose distinctions are taken or barred".
- "A loose distinction is never eligible" is right (FD 2.2).
- The FLOOR0 counterexample is correct; I checked it by hand (x17 + x18 + x19 = x0, so 0 is frozen and x1 = x2). It bears only on PO2, as the edge of B1.
- **PO2 has no run.** No row of the run table uses FLOOR0 or ONE-FEWER, and "changed by births of Y only" has no definition in D2.
- PO1: "receives" should be "takes". "Any set" should be the whole set, with a stated bound for the not-all-equal solver.

**B2**

- Right at the rule.
- With every choice read in full it is a proof: a renaming carries histories onto histories one to one.
- For drawn histories only the weighting is carried, not the counts. PO8 is a check where read in full (retiring, waiting) and a seeded replication under offshoots. Mark it so.

**B3**

- Nearly right. The trace cuts each met set down to X and its descendants. So a part wholly of X's descendants and the cut-down piece of a mixed part look the same in the trace. At the last round read, the traces can be equal while the parts differ (Y's birth takes a place of X's common knot in that round).
- Repair: record with each met set whether it had a member outside X and its descendants. Or keep P16 only on the parts by descent, where it is true by definition, and say so.
- The remark on values is right, and it is good news rather than a gap: a pattern that leaves two of a value need not depend on what Y is.
- "What is necessary is a take" is not proved. Keep it as seen in one case.

**The third-pattern runs**

- They show one more change under which the P6 case is lost, and that with Z barred the result follows the larger names. That is the choice's doing. They cannot show that Z did anything.
- Three-holder e changes the start beyond adding Z.
- The made-design construction will be triggered by the made-4 form case and has no start lists.

## 4. The inkling as registered

- **(i) is fair to his first sentence, with one caveat.** As seen, it is supported because there is no copier for even one member once the start is renamed. "Cannot be generalized" has that as a degenerate case. Report the two apart: no copier at all, or a copier for some members and not all.
- **(ii) does not honestly count as his second sentence.** His sentence has a copier as its object, and in the three cases X copies nothing.
  - One case is the control with Y the same as X.
  - The reverse happens in 14 runs against 3.
  - The made-4 case exists under parity only, so the cause is likely the implied closing.
  - This is two patterns changing each other's fresh counts. Register it under a neutral name ("X ended with Y making births, Y still making births") and do not let POA say "supported".
- **Plain sentences for the owner.**
  - As seen: "We have no copier yet, so there is nothing yet for a pattern to over-write or break out of. No fixed rule leaves two of every pattern in the class, nor of one once the start is renumbered. Under these laws nothing a pattern has is rewritten by another; only what it does next changes. In three runs the first pattern ends when the second keeps making knots and not when the second is stopped. The reverse happens in fourteen, and once between two patterns of the same kind. Rewriting was seen only under rations we do not use, and there the knot test fails."
  - A copier for some members and not all: "This is the outcome your inkling describes; here is the smallest pattern it fails on and what that pattern does to the copier's course."
  - A copier for the whole class: "Overturned for this class; nothing said beyond it."
  - No case of (ii): "Nothing we grew ends the other."
- **Sharper readings the registered runs can decide.** Register both as reported, with no prediction.
  - **(iii) One-way.** X's course differs with Y barred (confirmed through a meeting) and from X alone; Y's course is the same with X barred; Y makes a birth at T. Report the reverse and the controls. "What X does alone" is its renamed trace in B(i) and in X alone.
  - **(iv) On every case with two of Y** (stated rule or take list): with Z there, no two of Y; with Z barred, two again; no two of Z; Z makes a birth at T. This is reading 5 under its proper name. As seen it is 5 of 5 with Z named before Y, on a case that is supplied.

## 5. Predictions

- **Undecidable as registered:**
  - PO2 has no run.
  - PO3, PO4 and PO6 count 576 start runs over two namings of e, and PO7 needs made-2 with names exchanged. Run 2 has neither.
  - PO5 and PO6 list their runs fully only in the note, which the implementer will not have.
  - P4: run R's structures are not given.
  - P3: the record's CAP-3 counts are not given.
- **Pinned too exactly:** P15, PO3, PO4, PO5 and PO6 depend on the masks, the bound of 500 knots and T. Mark them as replications; a miss is a finding about the engines, not the claim. My sums agree: 828 = 48 + 168 + 140 + 0 + 252 + 220, and 550 + 94 + 180 + 4 = 828.
- **P9** says 3,000 histories; D2 registers 20,000. Small counts (made-3 has 4) make it fragile. Make it reported, or pool it.
- **True by construction but not marked:**
  - P20's first clause follows from P6.
  - P16 on parts by descent is true by definition.
  - PO8 is marked a check but is exact only where read in full.
- **P20's "reason"** must be stated as two checkable clauses: all three takes of round 3 take Y's fresh distinction; at round 6 the three are tied to three different start distinctions. Say "smallest in the registered class".
- **Still missing for his step 2:** P2 has the checks but not the sentence. With two holders, two loose distinctions tied to each other are the only loose distinctions of their connected structure, so two usable places need a third holder. State it, state the not-all-equal half, and report the holders of v in every values case.
- His stop is covered.

## 6. For the implementer

- **Not in what the implementer is given:**
  - `take_lists_v2.json` and its format.
  - Run R's structures.
  - The lists for two-knot, three-knot and three-knot-larger.
  - The record's CAP-3 counts.
  - The e-first starts and made-2 with names exchanged.
- **Reader controls:** Y and s on the two-knot start; the counting mode; the planted construction; rounds to 7 against the bound of 6.
- **Run 4:** D2 2.6 says "through the registered rounds"; the disclosure used s + 1 to s + 4. Also undefined:
  - the exact `<design>` and `<law name>` strings;
  - how a history stopped by the guard is counted;
  - which histories get knot tests.
- **Run 3:** "one part again by round 7" against 6 rounds; the pair-selection limits (FD 5.8 or not).
- **Renamings:**
  - n1 and n3 as exact label maps. On made designs the "blocks" are unequal and X is not a start block.
  - n4's exact call.
  - What "survives" compares.
- **The third pattern:** numeric labels for Z in both positions; made-design start lists and Z's h; when Z is barred; s for Z.
- **Descent** of knots made by round s (X's own, Y's own, start knots), needed for parts and for reading 2.
- **The fourth mark** on parts by descent, and X alone's comparison: say which renaming.
- **Masked runs** for Y against B_X.
- **The meeting round** when there is none.
- **Solver bounds** for PO1.
- **The naming convention:** D2 1.6 points to 4.5, which lists the renamings. The convention itself is FD 2.1 with e = 1000.

## 7. Words

- **"Ended by what it met"** is causal and needs no meeting as defined; fix as in 3.
- **"Goes on"** → "makes a birth in the last round read".
- **"Waits"** is fine as "every member left waits".
- **"The symmetric control"** names two things, one of which has no exchanging renaming. Use "the control with Y the same as X" and "a start with a renaming exchanging X and Y". "Exchange-symmetric" → "unchanged when X and Y are exchanged".
- **"Reader controls"** → "controls of the readings". Also rules as the subject of "read": "all four read names", "the numbering it reads", "MET's join clause and STEPS-1 read" → "use".
- **"The fourth mark"** now has two meanings (FD's and D2 5.3's). Use FD's name plus "on the replacement runs".
- **"Specific" and "specificity"** are a new noun not listed in D2 0. "One specific case" is ambiguous with "one particular case".
- **"Copier"** in "the start's copier", "three-knot copier" and "copier starts" breaks D2 0's own rule.
- **"Form" and "values"** are used outside his words ("form arm", "in values") against D2 0. Admit them there as labels of the readings.
- **"Crosses" and "crossing"** → "its way is" (FD's word).
- **Other replacements:**
  - "handed down a chain" → "handed on along";
  - "reaches two loose places" → "is tied at";
  - "planted" → "placed by hand";
  - "one bit" → "one value";
  - "X's chains" and "outputs" are undefined;
  - "stated by structure" → "stated without names";
  - "cheap" for ties is against FD's cost; give counts;
  - "permanent" → "at every later round";
  - "share" where counts are given → "counts".
- **Fine as they are:** "a third pattern", "descended from X only", "the take-by-take weighting", "present with X from round 0", "met by a dead knot", "hand on".

## 8. Verdict

Not as it is. Required, in order:

1. Register the arm's runs and listings in P2: e-first, made-2 with names exchanged, a FLOOR0/ONE-FEWER row, and the full PO5/PO6 lists and PO3 numbers.
2. POA: rename (ii), add (iii) and (iv), correct the plain sentence, and repair "ended", the round and the meeting condition.
3. B1 (c) and (d), and "never what it holds" in the claim and P2.
4. Values specificity; the base-law quantifier; the form class by family; the wording of the made-4 case, or its reverse check.
5. The B3 and P16 gap.
6. Everything in 6 that blocks the engine, starting with the files, the reader controls and the run 4 and run 3 round conflicts.
7. Mark PO8, P15, PO3 to PO6 and P9 for what they are.
8. Tie-freeness of the three-holder starts.
9. The step 2 sentence.
10. Words.

Optional:

- Form in run 4.
- The census by descent from X only.
- Holders of v in every values case.
- Rounds of ending in both runs.
- P20's clauses.
